REASONING:
**Step 1 – Frame the project**  
- **Objective:** Deploy a carbon capture, usage and storage (CCUS) cluster (HyNet) to capture CO₂ from industrial, hydrogen and waste sources, transport it via a T&S network and store it underground, supporting UK net‑zero, energy and economic security.  
- **Scope & components:** Anchor configuration – Eni (Transport & Storage Company, T&SCo), Essar Energy Transition Hydrogen (EETH) and Protos (Energy Recovery Facility). Build‑out projects (Padeswood, Viridor) are out‑of‑scope for this FBC but will join later. Initial network capacity 4.7 Mtpa (expandable to 10.5 Mtpa).  
- **Delivery model:** Regulated Asset Base (RAB) model for T&SCo administered by Ofgem; CfD‑type contracts for capture projects; government subsidies via Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) and Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA).  
- **Timeline:** FID sought now; anchor projects commissioned 2028; build‑out FIDs 2025‑2026; top‑up by 2030; expansion by 2034; major evaluations 2028‑2030 and post‑2030.  
- **Budget:** Total subsidy £9.1 bn (real 2021 prices); capital spend £4.1 bn (2024‑27) plus operational spend ≈ £11.1 bn (2028‑2050).  
- **Key stakeholders:** DESNZ (project sponsor), Ofgem (regulator), LCCC (contract counter‑party), Eni, EETH, Protos, UK Government (SoS, Chancellor), NSTA, OPRED, external advisors, local communities.  
- **External dependencies:** UK Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) carbon price, geological storage capacity, offshore pipeline construction, secondary legislation, subsidy‑control compliance.

**Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)**  

| Category | Candidate risk | Evidence (≤ 25 words) |
|---|---|---|
| technical | CO₂ leakage (high‑impact, low‑probability) | “government will underwrite several key high‑impact, low‑probability risks – principally relating to CO₂ leakage – via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA).” |
| technical | Network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects do not take FID | “risk that if one or more of the build‑out projects … fails to take FID, the network … will be under‑utilised.” |
| technical | Development costs for T&SCo could become nugatory | “risk that the T&SCo may incur some development costs which ultimately prove to be nugatory.” |
| technical | Construction cost overruns for Eni T&S network | “Eni T&S network construction overruns” (financial risk 6.7.11). |
| technical | Dense‑phase upgrade cost uncertainty (higher pressure injection) | “additional costs will be incurred in the 2030s as CO₂ is required to be injected at higher pressure (the HyNet dense phase transition).” |
| financial | Significant cost escalation since OBC | “While there has been significant cost escalation since the OBC, this has largely been driven by changes in underlying costs…” |
| financial | RSA shortfall if user fees < allowed revenue | “If there is a shortfall in demand … aggregate User fees do not meet the T&SCo’s allowed revenue, government will ‘top up’ these fees through the exchequer‑funded RSA.” |
| financial | Decommissioning fund shortfall | Listed under financial risks 5.7.5 “Decommissioning fund shortfall”. |
| financial | Fraud risk | Listed under financial risks 5.7.8 “Fraud”. |
| financial | Cross‑chain risk between T&SCo and capture projects | “cross‑chain risks from the interdependencies between the T&SCo and capture projects.” |
| schedule | Delay in finalising CCS Network Code (target July 2024) | “consensus on the full form CCS Network Code … expected by the end of July 24.” |
| schedule | Delay in FID‑critical secondary legislation | “Legislation overview: The programme has prioritised secondary legislation that is FID critical.” |
| schedule
